key_insight: VAE latents live on thin spherical shells and decoded perceptual/semantic content is carried mostly by direction (angle) rather than radius. Aligning latent geometry and performing flow matching that respects radial/angular structure prevents off-shell Euclidean transport and preserves semantics during generation.
problem_solved: Standard latent flow matching uses straight Euclidean paths that leave the thin-shell manifold of VAE latents, degrading decoded quality and interpolation fidelity; this work addresses the geometric mismatch between Gaussian noise and VAE latent shells.
method: Decompose each latent token into radial and angular components (radius vs direction) and use component-swap probes to show direction carries semantic/perceptual information.

Align latent geometry (match or normalize radii) and adapt flow-matching to operate on the spherical/angular component—transport along geometry-aware (e.g., great-circle) paths rather than Euclidean chords.
Combine radial handling and spherical flow matching in the latent pipeline so decoded images remain on-manifold and retain semantics during sampling and interpolation.
impact: By respecting latent spherical geometry, practitioners can get more semantically coherent interpolations and higher-fidelity samples from latent flow models with minimal changes to existing VAE+flow pipelines. This improves robustness and interpretability of latent-space operations.
visual_elements: Sphere diagram showing endpoints on a thin shell, comparing Euclidean chord vs geodesic (great-circle) transport paths.
Component-swap image grid: decode pairs where angle or radius is swapped to show which component controls semantics.
Pipeline schematic: VAE encoder → decompose (r, θ) → spherical flow matching → decoder, highlighting where geometry alignment occurs.
Quantitative bar/line chart mockup: metrics or qualitative comparisons (e.g., interpolation consistency, sample fidelity) before vs after geometry alignment.
paper_title: Aligning Latent Geometry for Spherical Flow Matching in Image Generation
paper_authors: Tuna Han Salih Meral, Kaan Oktay, Hidir Yesiltepe, Adil Kaan Akan, Pinar Yanardag
